source_en: Day 1 – Unknown (The sky looks like broken, fractured glass) 15:49. I'll never forget this number. Just one minute before the observation was complete, a dark rift suddenly tore open from the device in front of me, shredding the stream of data across the screen. My boots were still stuck to the lab floor, but my upper body had already been pulled into a strange, chaotic storm. That was the beginning. Now I find myself in a city I don't recognize, having just survived a bizarre Lament. It slices through buildings, people, space, everything two-dimensional, three-dimensional… and maybe things beyond that, though my eyes can't quite make sense of it anymore. My Forte is Sealing, something that might be considered a way to resist the passage of time. Maybe, if I keep trying, I can use it to record the abnormalities in this city and figure out how to break through it. I'm not going to sit here and wait for the end.
new_translation_vi: Ngày 1 – Không xác định (Bầu trời trông như thủy tinh vỡ, nứt nẻ) 15:49. Tớ sẽ không bao giờ quên con số này. Chỉ một phút trước khi quá trình quan sát hoàn tất, một vết nứt đen tối đột ngột xé toạc từ thiết bị trước mặt tớ, xé nát dòng dữ liệu trên màn hình. Đôi ủng của tớ vẫn dính chặt vào sàn phòng thí nghiệm, nhưng phần thân trên đã bị kéo vào một cơn bão kỳ lạ, hỗn loạn. Đó là sự khởi đầu. Giờ tớ thấy mình ở một thành phố tớ không nhận ra, vừa sống sót sau một trận Lament kỳ quái. Nó cắt xuyên qua các tòa nhà, con người, không gian, mọi thứ hai chiều, ba chiều… và có lẽ cả những thứ vượt xa hơn thế, mặc dù mắt tớ không còn hiểu được nữa. Forte của tớ là Phong ấn, thứ có thể được coi là một cách để chống lại sự trôi qua của thời gian. Có lẽ, nếu tớ tiếp tục cố gắng, tớ có thể sử dụng nó để ghi lại những bất thường trong thành phố này và tìm cách phá vỡ nó. Tớ sẽ không ngồi đây và chờ đợi sự kết thúc.

source_en: Day 7 – Cloudy (If what's above my head can still be called "weather.") When I woke up and checked my watch, I noticed something odd. Moss had started growing beneath the glass. This city, fractured and folded in on itself, seems trapped in some kind of temporal loop. Time moves forward and backward within a fixed range. But oddly enough, the plants don't seem bound by each "reset." The moss shouldn't be able to grow between the gears... unless time isn't flowing normally here. It's eroding, rushing, and spawning things that shouldn't even exist in the first place. Still, I'm grateful for this strange, unreasonable growth. It made me realize this city isn't beyond saving. There is a way out. (The pen seems to pause, leaving a small blot of ink on the paper.) There's one thing I still can't let go of. That rift... In my blurred memory, it sealed shut almost as soon as I was pulled into the storm. But if I can't figure out what caused it, or how to stop it. There's no way to guarantee it won't open again. And if it does... someone else could get dragged in. However, time's against me.
new_translation_vi: Ngày 7 – Nhiều mây (Nếu những gì trên đầu tớ vẫn có thể gọi là "thời tiết.") Khi tớ thức dậy và kiểm tra đồng hồ, tớ nhận thấy điều gì đó kỳ lạ. Rêu đã bắt đầu mọc dưới lớp kính. Thành phố này, bị nứt nẻ và gấp khúc, dường như bị mắc kẹt trong một loại vòng lặp thời gian nào đó. Thời gian di chuyển tiến và lùi trong một phạm vi cố định. Nhưng kỳ lạ thay, thực vật dường như không bị ràng buộc bởi mỗi lần "thiết lập lại". Rêu không nên mọc được giữa các bánh răng... trừ khi thời gian không trôi bình thường ở đây. Nó đang xói mòn, vội vã và sinh ra những thứ thậm chí không nên tồn tại ngay từ đầu. Tuy nhiên, tớ biết ơn sự phát triển kỳ lạ, vô lý này. Nó khiến tớ nhận ra thành phố này không phải là không thể cứu vãn. Có một lối thoát. (Cây bút dường như dừng lại, để lại một vệt mực nhỏ trên giấy.) Có một điều tớ vẫn không thể buông bỏ. Vết nứt đó... Trong ký ức mờ nhạt của tớ, nó đã đóng lại ngay khi tớ bị kéo vào cơn bão. Nhưng nếu tớ không thể tìm ra nguyên nhân gây ra nó, hoặc cách ngăn chặn nó. Không có cách nào đảm bảo nó sẽ không mở ra lần nữa. Và nếu nó mở ra... ai đó khác có thể bị kéo vào. Tuy nhiên, thời gian không đứng về phía tớ.

source_en: Day 136 – Abnormal Pressure (If this constant pressure in my ears counts as such) Among the supplies Chisa brought back today was a can of oranges, the label printed with a production date long past... but that hardly matters anymore. These so-called "foods" are really just compressed Remnant Energy. Chisa gave the can to me. She sat off to the side with a piece of spring steel she'd salvaged, slicing it into a curved blade using her Forte, turning it into a new weapon. Watching her, I suddenly recalled another day. She was sitting just like this, halfway through organizing supplies on the sofa, when she turned and asked me what my Forte really was. I showed her a small amber, the one containing a preserved memory of the first time we worked together at this home base: the lights were dim, she was repairing a weapon, and I was taking notes on anomalies in the city's time flow. It was a rare, peaceful night, as long as we could ignore the fact that we were still trapped in a city sealed off from the outside world. To hold out against the erratic occurrences of the Lament, I once tried to learn Chisa's practical skills, but I failed. Of course I did. Still, she taught me a few special ways to leave markings. I remember what she said back then: "Stop treating everything like a science experiment. Think of every piece of scrap metal as a blade that never misses—" (The pen pierced the page, leaving a blot of ink.) And I know she truly meant it. This city, drenched in Lament, is riddled with danger. And yet, she always throws herself forward to shield everyone else. She thinks I haven't noticed how much she's burning herself out... doesn't know her body's running at the edge of collapse. But I've done the calculations many times. I know exactly how long she has before she crosses the breaking point. The only good thing is that this Sonoro seems to have stalled time and her condition. But I can't let her stay like this forever. I want to take her back. Back to the Black Shores, to the people I trust. There has to be a solution waiting there. I'll bring her back. No matter the cost.
new_translation_vi: Ngày 136 – Áp suất bất thường (Nếu áp suất không đổi trong tai tớ được tính là như vậy) Trong số những nguồn cung cấp mà Chisa mang về hôm nay có một lon cam, nhãn in ngày sản xuất đã lâu... nhưng điều đó chẳng còn quan trọng nữa. Những thứ gọi là "thực phẩm" này thực chất chỉ là Năng lượng Tàn dư bị nén lại. Chisa đã đưa lon đó cho tớ. Cô ấy ngồi sang một bên với một mảnh thép lò xo mà cô ấy đã thu hồi được, cắt nó thành một lưỡi dao cong bằng Forte của mình, biến nó thành một vũ khí mới. Nhìn cô ấy, tớ chợt nhớ lại một ngày khác. Cô ấy cũng ngồi như thế này, đang sắp xếp đồ tiếp tế trên ghế sofa, khi cô ấy quay lại và hỏi tớ Forte thực sự của tớ là gì. Tớ cho cô ấy xem một mảnh hổ phách nhỏ, mảnh chứa ký ức được bảo tồn về lần đầu tiên chúng ta làm việc cùng nhau tại căn cứ này: ánh đèn mờ ảo, cô ấy đang sửa vũ khí, và tớ đang ghi chép về những bất thường trong dòng thời gian của thành phố. Đó là một đêm yên bình hiếm hoi, miễn là chúng ta có thể phớt lờ thực tế rằng chúng ta vẫn bị mắc kẹt trong một thành phố bị phong tỏa khỏi thế giới bên ngoài. Để chống lại những sự kiện thất thường của Lament, tớ từng cố gắng học các kỹ năng thực tế của Chisa, nhưng tớ đã thất bại. Tất nhiên là tớ thất bại rồi. Tuy nhiên, cô ấy đã dạy tớ một vài cách đặc biệt để leave các dấu hiệu. Tớ nhớ những gì cô ấy nói hồi đó: "Đừng coi mọi thứ như một thí nghiệm khoa học. Hãy coi mỗi mảnh kim loại vụn là một lưỡi kiếm không bao giờ trượt—" (Cây bút đâm xuyên qua trang giấy, để lại một vệt mực.) Và tớ biết cô ấy thực sự có ý đó. Thành phố này, đẫm trong Lament, đầy rẫy nguy hiểm. Tuy nhiên, cô ấy luôn lao về phía trước để bảo vệ mọi người. Cô ấy nghĩ tớ không nhận ra cô ấy đã burning bản thân mình đến mức nào... không biết cơ thể cô ấy đang chạy ở ngưỡng sụp đổ. Nhưng tớ đã tính toán nhiều lần. Tớ biết chính xác cô ấy còn bao lâu trước khi vượt qua điểm giới hạn. Điều tốt duy nhất là Sonoro này dường như đã làm chậm thời gian và tình trạng của cô ấy. Nhưng tớ không thể để cô ấy ở lại đây mãi mãi. Tớ muốn đưa cô ấy trở lại. Trở lại Black Shores, với những người tớ tin tưởng. Chắc chắn phải có một giải pháp đang chờ đợi ở đó. Tớ sẽ đưa cô ấy trở lại. Bất kể giá nào.

source_en: Day 159 – Sunny (A rare clear day) Today, Chisa told me she found a new spot that could serve as a base—an old, spacious cafe. From the large terrace on the second floor, you can see a beautiful view of the city center. It's been a long time since I've seen her this excited. It feels like we're one step closer to breaking the loop. And in fact, we are making progress. (The handwriting sharpens slightly.) Based on my research over the past few days, I'm now fairly certain of this: the key to unraveling this endless Möbius loop lies at the heart of the city—Neon Tower. It is the center of the Lament. The origin. And most importantly, the point that lies closest to the outside world. If we can reach the top, perhaps we'll be able to contact the people back at the Black Shores. Perhaps that's the way out of this Sonoro. The moss has already crept past the gears of my watch and reached the surface. Still, I haven't replaced it. It reminds me of time... and that something can keep pushing through falsehoods until it reaches the truth. I'll head for the heart of Neon Tower tomorrow morning. If time here is clay, then I will mold it into a road, one that leads us home.
new_translation_vi: Ngày 159 – Nắng (Một ngày quang đãng hiếm hoi) Hôm nay, Chisa nói với tớ rằng cô ấy đã tìm thấy một địa điểm mới có thể làm căn cứ—một quán cà phê cũ, rộng rãi. Từ sân thượng lớn trên tầng hai, cậu có thể nhìn thấy khung cảnh tuyệt đẹp của trung tâm thành phố. Đã lâu rồi tớ mới thấy cô ấy phấn khích như vậy. Cảm giác như chúng ta đã tiến gần hơn một bước đến việc phá vỡ vòng lặp. Và thực tế là, chúng ta đang đạt được tiến bộ. (Chữ viết sắc nét hơn một chút.) Dựa trên nghiên cứu của tớ trong vài ngày qua, tớ khá chắc chắn về điều này: chìa khóa để tháo gỡ vòng lặp Möbius vô tận này nằm ở trung tâm thành phố—Neon Tower. Đó là trung tâm của Lament. Nguồn gốc. Và quan trọng nhất, điểm nằm gần thế giới bên ngoài nhất. Nếu chúng ta có thể lên đến đỉnh, có lẽ chúng ta sẽ có thể liên lạc với những người ở Black Shores. Có lẽ đó là lối thoát khỏi Sonoro này. Rêu đã bò qua các bánh răng của đồng hồ tớ và chạm tới bề mặt. Tuy nhiên, tớ vẫn chưa thay thế nó. Nó nhắc tớ về thời gian... và rằng một thứ gì đó có thể tiếp tục đẩy qua những điều giả dối cho đến khi nó chạm tới sự thật. Tớ sẽ hướng tới trung tâm Neon Tower vào sáng mai. Nếu thời gian ở đây là đất sét, thì tớ sẽ nặn nó thành một con đường, con đường dẫn chúng ta về nhà.

source_en: (The handwriting is noticeably rushed.) It should be around noon. I've reached the third floor of Neon Tower. Rubble from the buildings is scattered and floating around like a shattered kaleidoscope. Some pieces have even stuck to my clothes. I must look like I'm covered in rainbow frosting. …But my body is getting colder. Turns out I was right. Either these "sugar crystals" or the entire city are slowly draining the body heat of anyone who doesn't belong here. I need to keep moving. I have to find the right path to the top, and fast.
new_translation_vi: (Chữ viết rõ ràng là vội vã.) Khoảng giữa trưa rồi. Tớ đã lên đến tầng ba của Neon Tower. Gạch vụn từ các tòa nhà nằm rải rác và trôi nổi xung quanh như một chiếc kính vạn hoa bị vỡ. Một vài mảnh thậm chí còn dính vào quần áo tớ. Chắc tớ trông như thể bị phủ đầy kem cầu vồng vậy. …Nhưng cơ thể tớ đang lạnh dần. Hóa ra tớ đã đúng. Hoặc là những "tinh thể đường" này hoặc toàn bộ thành phố đang dần rút cạn nhiệt độ cơ thể của bất kỳ ai không thuộc về nơi này. Tớ cần tiếp tục di chuyển. Tớ phải tìm đúng con đường lên đỉnh, và thật nhanh.

source_en: 15:23. It's been five full hours since I entered the Tower. Nearly half of that time was wasted, because I took the wrong path forward. My watch is almost entirely covered by moss. It spread so quickly. There's no doubt now. Time inside the Tower flows differently from the outside… No, the entire city of Honami is out of sync. I passed through countless time fragments, saw my tenth birthday party cake, the balloons and flowers from my coming-of-age ceremony, and the lab coat I first wore when I joined the Black Shores. It was happiness. Surreal like a dream… But I couldn't let myself get lost in it. I took off my protective gloves and ran my fingers across the corroded surfaces, trying to touch the reality in front of me. Surprisingly, it felt warm, like the vein of some living creature. (The writing wavers here, as if the hand holding the pen had started to shake.) …Or maybe that warmth was a hallucination born out of being so cold. My mind is slipping, but I can't stop now. I knew from the start this would never be an easy path... But so what? Even the most dangerous equation still needs someone willing to solve it.
new_translation_vi:
15:23. Đã năm tiếng đồng hồ trôi qua kể từ khi tớ vào Tháp. Gần một nửa thời gian đó đã bị lãng phí, vì tớ đã chọn sai đường.

Đồng hồ của tớ gần như bị rêu bao phủ hoàn toàn. Nó lan nhanh quá. Giờ thì không còn nghi ngờ gì nữa. Thời gian bên trong Tháp trôi khác với bên ngoài… Không, toàn bộ thành phố Honami đang bị lệch nhịp. Tớ đã đi qua vô số mảnh thời gian, nhìn thấy chiếc bánh sinh nhật lần thứ mười của mình, những quả bóng bay và hoa từ lễ trưởng thành, và chiếc áo khoác phòng thí nghiệm tớ mặc lần đầu tiên khi gia nhập Black Shores.
\

source_en: (The handwriting is distorted, yet forceful, pressing deep into the page.) Endless fragments of time... I didn't expect to witness my entire life play out in this place. Honestly? It was a good life. The repeated crossings and the blurring of my senses have made it impossible to judge the passage of time. Even the hands on my watch have stopped at last, caught in the moss's hold. But that's okay. I achieved my goal. After countless trial and error, I've finally mapped out every correct path. I know I probably won't make it to the top though... It doesn't matter. Even if I don't live to see the end, it doesn't matter. All I ever wanted was to lay down a clear road, so those who come after can walk across my bones and reach the light. That's enough for me. In fact… (The next words are nearly illegible, the ink smudged by a trembling hand.) I feel content. I remember that night when I was eighteen. I'd just passed the Black Shores assessment. I stood overlooking the sea by the Haven of Sprouts, gazing up at the sky. Back then, I believed the truth was hidden beyond the stars. Now I'm curled up inside the steel maze of Neon Tower, watching the Lament tear space part. Watching fragments of my past, my whole life... I've never been this close to the truth. Across time, I reach out to my eighten-year-old self. Space collapses around me. My mind catches fire in the light. I feel myself unraveling, being stripped away, broken down, and engraved. Then I hear my eighteen-year-old voice saying: "So you really made it here."

All I ever wanted was to lay down a clear road, so those who come after can walk across my bones and reach the light. That's enough for me. In fact… (The next words are nearly illegible, the ink smudged by a trembling hand.) I feel content. I remember that night when I was eighteen. I'd just passed the Black Shores assessment. I stood overlooking the sea by the Haven of Sprouts, gazing up at the sky. Back then, I believed the truth was hidden beyond the stars. Now I'm curled up inside the steel maze of Neon Tower, watching the Lament tear space part. Watching fragments of my past, my whole life... I've never been this close to the truth. Across time, I reach out to my eighten-year-old self. Space collapses around me. My mind catches fire in the light. I feel myself unraveling, being stripped away, broken down, and engraved. Then I hear my eighteen-year-old voice saying: "So you really made it here."

source_en:
[This manual is distributed by the Chamber of Enlightenment to all stationed Acolytes. For internal reference only. Unauthorized reproduction, transcription, or circulation is strictly prohibited.]
 
Septimont—A City of Warriors Where Faith Runs Thin
 
In ancient times, Ragunna and Septimont were among the earliest settlements during the Age of a Thousand Islands. The conflicts in that distant age drove a wedge between the two, leading them down separate paths and shaping two distinct societies with their own customs and cultures. Unlike Ragunna, the Sentinel's blessings have not reached Septimont, for its people long ago abandoned their faith. Septimontians regard miracles and divine grace with indifference, placing their reverence instead in strength and valor. They venerate heroes born of war and the hunt, and revel in gladiating games that verge on barbarism.
 
It is worth noting, however, that these practices do not stem from disrespect. Septimontians believe the Sentinel to be a supreme hero and leader, worthy of unparalleled glory. They revere the Sentinel and sing of ancient legends, aspiring one day to stand alongside Them and achieve unmatched feats. Such thinking is an absolute transgression against the Sentinel, and we must guard ourselves vigilantly against it.
 
Septimontians have demonstrated their indifference toward the Sentinel and the Order's teachings by allowing temples to fall into ruin and altars to be dismantled. Yet the Order has remained patient and generous. Trade now flourishes between Ragunna and Septimont, and within the city itself, devoted Acolytes continue to preach and spread the Sentinel's divine grace.
 
...
 
All Acolytes stationed abroad must uphold the Sentinel's teachings, observe discretion and restraint, and respect Septimont's local customs to avoid unnecessary conflict. Should they face strong resistance, they may present their official credentials or, if necessary, request intervention from the Order's External Affairs Department.

source_en:
Long ago, it was right at this solemn and sacred site of trial that the Blessed Maiden was bestowed Haultir, the Sword of Virtue. Now, in the same hallowed place, the Blessed Maiden raised the Sword of Virtue high, her gaze fixed upon the squire kneeling before her. The squire held his posture with perfect stillness, silent as a statue.
 
"Before our Master Imperator, do you vow to fight only for justice and righteousness, and to lend your hand to the weak?"
 
The squire could not speak. He answered with a slow, deliberate nod.
 
"Do you vow to remain steadfast in faith and oath, never to abandon the duties entrusted to you?"
 
Again, the squire nodded.
 
"Even should you find yourself in the most dire of trials? Even should you... face death itself?"
 
The squire uttered an indistinct sound. From the tone, it seemed to be an affirmation.
 
The flat of the Sword of Virtue lightly touched Cadanto's shoulders—once, twice, thrice.
 
"From this day forth, you are a true knight, Cadanto."
 
For many of the Acolytes witnessing the ceremony, this was the first time they had seen an <ano=Divine envoy>Echo</ano> rise to knighthood.

source_en:
...
 
As the Sword of Virtue touched Cadanto's chestplate, the duel between the Blessed Maiden and her Echo came to an end.
 
Cadanto knelt humbly in defeat. The crowd, who had been holding their breath, erupted into thunderous applause. At that moment, an Acolyte led a young girl through the excited crowd. Dressed in commoner's clothes, the girl clutched a large bouquet of blooming Firecracker Jewelweeds. The bundle was almost taller than she was. 
 
A gift for the Blessed Maiden, I assumed. Ever since she began her studies in Avinoleum, devotees had begun to make long journeys just to catch a glimpse of the girl blessed by the Sentinel. But this girl merely nodded toward the Blessed Maiden before turning toward Cadanto.
 
To everyone's surprise, the girl presented the bouquet to him. After some explanation from the Acolyte, we learned that Cadanto had recently saved a family from Tacet Discords near Avinoleum's outskirts. The towering Echo knight remained half-kneeling and silent. He didn't seem to understand why a human would offer him flowers, or perhaps he felt unworthy of such thanks?
 
"So this is what you've been doing in my absence…" The Blessed Maiden smiled warmly. "Cadanto, accept the flowers. You've earned them."
 
Still silent, the knight laid down his greatsword and carefully received the bouquet. The little girl immediately leaned forward and embraced him, pressing her face against his cold armor. As always, Cadanto wordlessly bore both her tearful thanks and joyful sobs.
 
Cadanto… as many have said, is the Blessed Maiden's loyal servant and shield. But he is also a blade that protects the people.
 
...
 
[Note: This manuscript is scheduled for official publication following the Blessed Maiden's coronation ceremony. Special thanks to Avinoleum for their generous assistance during our research.]

source_en:
(This appears to be a personal memoir written by the now-retired Acolyte Julia, recounting her experiences and reflections while working at the Titular Repository.)
 
"Excuse me... I'd like to read this book. Do I need to register here?"
 
Accompanying the timid voice before me was a biography, its cover bearing the portrait of the Blessed Maiden. I looked up from the desk and saw a small girl with pale violet curls. There was a mole just beneath one of her eyes. Tiny and delicate. Her skin was so pale that it was nearly translucent like someone who hadn't seen sunlight in a very long time.
 
"You're free to read anything here. Just remember to put the books away when you're done," I said as gently as I could, worried the solemn atmosphere of the library might frighten her away.
 
She was clearly not an Avinoleum student, yet she began appearing regularly in the library in the days that followed. She wandered between the circular shelves, always quietly absorbed in whatever book she picked up. Sometimes she asked me to help her find specific texts. Some were dense theological books, while others were thick volumes on the ocean or pharmacology—not quite the usual interests for someone her age. We grew acquainted. I learned that she'd been brought to Avinoleum by her relatives. They had their own matters to attend to and left her to wander freely in this comparatively safe library.
 
Her departure was as sudden as her arrival. That afternoon, as if answering some unseen summons, she closed the book in her hands and slid it back onto the shelf. I remember it. It was a study of the traditions of the Blessed Maiden in Ragunna. In the slanting dusk light, a long shadow stretched across the floor. Her guardian, presumably.
 
"Thank you for looking after me these past few days." She stood in front of me, doing her best to smile. "Cantarella... I'm Cantarella Fisalia."
 
That surname explained a great many things. Her belated introduction. The sorrow hidden in her words. The flicker of bitterness as she looked toward the door. I rose and took her hand. At the very least, I didn't want her to feel alone on the walk back to the threshold.

source_en:
To all Acolytes, faculty and students:
 
Recently, the Seminary has discovered instances of students bringing dragon Echoes into the Titular Repository and the dormitory quarters without permission, resulting in considerable chaos. In order to ensure a safe and quiet academic environment and to reaffirm reverence for the Divine Envoys, the following provisional regulations are hereby issued for all enrolled students:
 
1. Dragon Echoes should not be taken out of Zargon Garden without permission.
 
 2. The use of Fortes within designated Echo gathering zones in Zargon Garden is strictly prohibited. (Specific boundaries attached separately.)
 
3. Close contact with dragon Echoes is forbidden unless officially reported and approved. This includes, but is not limited to, feeding, teasing, or challenging them in any form.
 
During non-Carnevale periods, violators will face confinement ranging from two to five days. Repeat or severe offenders will incur escalated penalties in accordance with the Student Handbook. Regulations specific to the Carnevale period will be issued separately.
 
Praise be to Imperator.
Avinoleum Office of Academic Affairs

source_en:
(Most of the contents have been lost. Only the preface remains relatively intact.)
 
You'll easily pick out students from the Fisalia family at the Seminary.
 
Not because there are many of them, but because they simply stand out. Fisalia students tend to be brooding and solitary, always slightly apart from the energy around them. Just as people from Ragunna expect them to be.
 
Among students, rumors circulate: that the Fisalias poison their own meals to build resistance, that they travel via an underground cable car, and that they swim like fish. Only one of these is untrue. Still, the fact that people believe them shows how deep prejudice runs, even here at Avinoleum, where elites from all corners gather.
 
I'm not from the Fisalia family myself, but I've befriended several. These Avinoleum-based Fisalians live closer to the family's ancient mission than most of their kin. As our bond deepened, a question began to take root in me, growing into an uncontrollable curiosity: Why does this venerable, illustrious family endure society's slander without protest? They no longer argue. They keep their silence. Only in their troubled dreams might you catch a whisper—broken phrases—hinting at the truth behind the veil.
 
What are the Fisalias hiding? Or rather, what have they been carrying? The events and interviews collected in this book have been recorded with the consent of those involved, with sensitive details omitted. If, by the end of this book, you find yourself with a different understanding of the Fisalias, then this work will have served its purpose.
 
...

source_en:
The bastard and that lapdog of hers are still on my tail. But this is as far as I can go for now. I need to rest. My right hand hurts so much I think it might be broken. As for my mind... I still feel dazed, but already much clearer than before. I thought I was losing it... I need to sit here for a while. Here's hoping those traps can buy me some time...

Soon I'll be able to see the sun, see the moon... the skies. Sometimes I forget I once belonged there, a place with sunlight and order. And here? Even the air reeks with despair... By Imperator, may this cursed dump and all its evil slowly rot in these dark sewers.

I couldn't find Brandon, but I have a feeling he was here—I can't tell if it's a hunch or if I'm being delusional. He must've made it out already... Yeah, that's right. The fellow's got more tricks up his sleeves than I do. He must've dropped his ID card in those vents as a distraction. Even got me fooled. Just like when we played pool... And here I am worrying about him. Ha, I'm such an idiot.

It's fine, I'll be out soon enough. Brandon, when I find you... I'm going to give you a good punch in the face. Just you wait.

source_en:
Corned Tumbleyak – Seven jars. Hubert found them in a storage room piled with junk, and Sentinel knows how long they'd been there. He says this stuff must've been sitting there since the Dark Tide, at least twenty years ago. Must be emergency supplies people stocked up out of panic. Good thing they packed the jars with salt, so they're still edible.

Pickled Fish – Sixteen jars. Brandon gathered a group and fished them out of the sewers leading to the sea while those masks weren't looking. Gotta keep these jars hidden, or else they'll be taken away like the rest of our food if they find them.

source_en:
That woman who calls herself Talos took all of our food and forced us to obey her commands. She said this was the way of the Black Alley of old, where strength determines power and wealth, and the weak have no place. This order existed ten, twenty years ago, and even long before that. Brandon and the others tried to challenge her, hoping to liberate us from her "rule," but they failed. That was the last anyone ever saw of them.

Oh, I've heard plenty of stories about the Black Alley, all right. The evil they committed. How they eventually received the judgment and punishment they had coming for them. All we wanted was a peaceful life in the Black Alley. We never wanted to be like them, wreaking havoc in the city. We just want to live our own lives here. The Black Alley is our home.

I have a plan in mind. If all goes well, then I can escape this miserable dump. I heard that a hero named the "Blazing Nightwalker" took out the previous gang. Maybe I can find her and ask her to save the Black Alley again.

Talos sent me to the city on errands for the next couple of days, so you're in charge while I'm gone, rookie.
Don't sweat it. Just follow my instructions to the letter, and you won't screw this up.

We open for business after six in the evening. During the day, put those kids on cleaning duty and make sure the broken bottles and mess from the night before are taken care of. No one likes a messy establishment. The Black Alley doesn't get any sunlight, so keep an eye on your watch and don't miss opening time.

Once people start to come in, hit the green button twice. Start things off with a track to set the mood. And remember: don't serve beverages just yet. If someone decides to make a scene about it, have Vincent take them to the ring and settle it over fists. If Vincent can't handle it, call Talos.

After a twenty-minute warmup, hit the red button once and the green button twice. Repeat this every half hour. I've prepped some banger music that they'll love. This is when you have the boys bring out the drinks. Once the vibe picks up, that's when the booze starts selling.

Keep in mind, whenever you see Talos show up, hit the yellow button right away. That'll play her favorite rock song, "The Black Alley Devils."

That's about it. She's all yours, rookie!

Once people start to come in, hit the green button twice. Start things off with a track to set the mood. And remember: don't serve beverages just yet. If someone decides to make a scene about it, have Vincent take them to the ring and settle it over fists. If Vincent can't handle it, call Talos.

After a twenty-minute warmup, hit the red button once and the green button twice. Repeat this every half hour. I've prepped some banger music that they'll love. This is when you have the boys bring out the drinks. Once the vibe picks up, that's when the booze starts selling.

Keep in mind, whenever you see Talos show up, hit the yellow button right away. That'll play her favorite rock song, "The Black Alley Devils."

That's about it. She's all yours, rookie!

source_en:
This is my fifth day in the Black Alley. People here are always on edge like they're afraid of something. No one says a word about it, of course.

The Black Alley is an oddity to the Ragunnesi. Youngsters these days don't even know it exists, while the old consider it a forbidden territory. Imagine the uproar it would cause in Ragunna if I wrote about its secrets and published them!

I met a nice fellow—everyone calls him the Runner, although I'm not sure who's pulling his strings. Thanks to his help, I got access to the Black Alley and its many mysteries.

The first three days of my investigation came up empty. But I did get to know a young man named Brandon over a game of pool. Seems like he's spent his fair share of time here. To be honest, he's damn good at the game, a worthy opponent, as long as he isn't cheating. Last time we played, the coat I had hanging nearby suddenly started burning. Luckily, I put it out in time, but by the time I came back, he had "scored" three points while I was gone.

Brandon is really tight-lipped about the Black Alley and always seems preoccupied with something. Still, I believe he could be the breakthrough I need in my investigation. He's not as stubborn as the old timers, nor as much of a pain to talk to as those masks. I still can't figure out where they came from. Maybe I'll figure it out someday.

Speaking of which, I haven't seen Brandon for two days. Maybe he went to help the starving old folks. As I learned during my investigation, the people here scrape by with odd jobs, barely managing to get enough food. Brandon is always sharing his rations with them.

Wherever he's gone, he'll be back for more pool. All I need to do is wait for him.

[Today's Drink Specials]
Vent-a-Nite: Made with aged liquor as the base, infused with refreshing herbal extracts. One sip will send a cool rush from head to toe, like stepping into a ventilation shaft after an ice-cold shower!
Recommendation: ☆☆☆☆

Dragon's Breath Octane: Featuring Pavo Plum juice swiped from the docks and a spoonful of real fossil fuel, this fiery mix is for the boldest drinkers! Dare your friends to survive the burning journey from throat to stomach. First one to take a sip of water picks up the tab!
Recommendation: ☆☆☆

Biohoard: A concoction made from pickled fish and corned meat juices. Tastes just as bad as it smells. I don't know how anyone could enjoy this, but it was made on request from an anonymous letter... Anyway, makes for a good prank on your friends!
Recommendation: ☆
To the anonymous requester: Your drink is ready. Please pay for it soon, or I'll tell Talos and she'll find out who sent this letter.

Golden Hour Special: A special blend of Tumbleyak butter and Nectarwine. A perfect fusion of the rustic charm of Whisperwind Haven and the sophisticated taste of the Montelli Quarters. Some might find it lacking a bold kick, but trust me, the creamy bubbles and velvety texture will win you over.
Recommendation: ☆☆☆☆☆

source_en:
Brandon's not the only one who's gone missing. People have been disappearing left and right. Good thing I learned how to quickly memorize people's faces in school, otherwise I could've easily overlooked this.

Everyone here seems indifferent to these disappearances. They're not even remotely curious about where those people went, or what fate they'll suffer. They just go about their business numbly while enduring the dwindling food supply.

As for those masks, I'm now certain they're working for some bigshot who recently showed up in the Black Alley. They occasionally leave to return to Ragunna City. I try to keep my distance, but I once overheard something during one of their gatherings... they're a bunch of criminals. Thugs. They were in one helluva celebratory mood talking about the "rebirth of the Black Alley." Whoever their boss is, she seems to be planning on making her fortune through crime.

But then what? What happens after the rebirth of the Black Alley? I haven't the slightest clue. To be honest, I normally consider myself a brave person, but I'm scared. Scared of that boss of theirs. Scared of her plans... I just want to leave now. Let the Chamber of Discipline deal with these criminals.

I did make an unexpected discovery today, though I can't tell if it's good news or bad news. I found an ID card in a tunnel near the ventilation shafts, something the residents of the Black Alley use to identify each other. It belongs to Brandon.

Did something happen to him? Or maybe... he left it there on purpose as some kind of guide? Or as a warning? Those masks are watching every move I make, I can't just make a break for it. Maybe Brandon knows a way out. I have to find him.

Talos had me and a group of guys on fixing and patching duty. Including the flooded area out front. The amount of effort it took to figure out how this drainage system works was something else. That thing that looks like a spiral staircase is actually a dead drainage outlet. I spent some time rerouting a power line to it, and now it's working properly.

<color=yellow>There's an outlet on the central rotating column. Hit the switch and it activates. Once the water is drained, the path beneath will be accessible.</color>

Best not to activate it unless absolutely necessary. Talos said it's the last line of defense against any intruders trying to get too deep into the Black Alley, so just keep it flooded unless our guys need to pass through.

source_en:
I saw what happened to those who disappeared. I can't stay here any longer. The air here reeks of madness. I'm scared... scared that if I stay here, I'll become one of them. Cruel, twisted, with a complete disregard for the law.

How long have I been here? There's no sense of day or night down in these sewers. A week? A month? Maybe by the time I make it out of here, Ragunna City will already be a burning ruin with only the criminals left, throwing an endless carnival of destruction and evil.

They will destroy me and the city. Not even the sea can douse the hellfire in their hearts. It'll rage through the ruins, and we'll all burn to nothing... 

Imperator protect me... Yes, that's right. There's still hope. They'll protect my body and soul... They will.

I have a duty now. As a student. A journalist. And a believer. I... I must leave here, tell everyone the truth, and stop Talos before she poisons us all with her evil.

...And yes, I understand. I might die in the process, or even worse... if they catch me... But I can't just watch and let it all unfold. Damn it, legs! Move! Now's not the time...

They're being called away by Talos... Now's my chance. Fewer eyes on me. It has to be Brandon... I knew it. He drew them away.

I've got a knife hidden. Today's the day I've been waiting for. I've hidden voice recordings all over the Black Alley. If something happens to me, those who come after will know what happened here. Courage... Yes, only courage, the most precious human quality... can put an end to this madness.

Oh, great Imperator, grant me mercy from the high heavens. May your gaze forever watch over your believers, and grace them with courage and victory. May your light disperse the darkness looming over this place. And may justice descend upon the mortal world through your wings...

The path lies hidden within the blessings... The messengers, though extraordinary, are not without flaws. To proceed, one must present that which can heal their hearts.

<color=yellow>The messenger on the left has lost their way, unable to escape the mire.</color>
<color=yellow>The messenger in the center is scarred by betrayal, their heart sealed because of it.</color>
<color=yellow>The messenger on the right has achieved nothing, forever consumed by doubt.</color>

Present your qualities before them to restore their wholeness.

(Below the inscription are drawings of three human figures in different poses, labeled "Loyalty," "Guidance," and "Recognition." These could be clues to solving the puzzle.)

source_en:
<color=Highlight>Titular Repository Memoir - Part I</color>
"(This appears to be a personal memoir written by the now-retired Acolyte Julia. Most pages have been lost.)
 
That day, I recognized a familiar figure by the shelves in the Titular Repository. As I'd done in my youth, I tapped his shoulder. Andrea turned, recognized me, and murmured, "Teacher." He looked just as I remembered from our last meeting, yet years had slipped by unnoticed. He had come all this way just to see me. We found a quiet corner to talk.
 
Andrea spoke of his time as a traveling Acolyte, carrying the Sentinel's blessings beyond Ragunna to Riccioli, Septimont, Lilyland... through lands rich and poor, faithful and faithless. His journey must have been arduous yet extraordinary. The new wrinkles and scars on his face told me he was no longer that headstrong young man driven only by passion. His faith and ideals had forged him into a weathered knight.
 
But then, he began to confess. Not about duty, but about his daughter. It was the confession of a father, burdened with guilt toward a daughter he had failed. That kind of regret shouldn't have belonged to an Acolyte, so I did not offer the Sentinel's absolution in Their stead. The same devotion still shimmered in his eyes, and I knew he would continue traveling. Still a devout Acolyte. Still an absent father.
 
So I told him I was writing this memoir. I want to record my experiences here in Avinoleum, and in this very library. Most of them are trivial, yet each is a vivid reflection of the era I live in. These forgotten corners of history deserve to be remembered. The Sentinel teaches us to illuminate the world for others, and it's also important not to forget to light the way for those closest to us.
 
<color=Highlight>Titular Repository Memoir - Part II</color>

"…
 
On an otherwise ordinary closing day, I was carrying a stack of old books across the platform outside the library when I was drawn, almost involuntarily, into a crowd of onlookers. A duel held every gaze. As the Sword of Virtue touched Cadanto's breastplate, the match between Blessed Maiden and Echo came to an end.
 
Cadanto knelt humbly in defeat. The crowd, who had been holding their breath, erupted into thunderous applause. At that moment, an Acolyte led a young girl through the excited crowd. Dressed in commoner's clothes, the girl clutched a large bouquet of blooming Firecracker Jewelweeds. The bundle was almost taller than she was.
 
A gift for the Blessed Maiden, I assumed. Ever since she began her studies in Avinoleum, devotees had begun to make long journeys just to catch a glimpse of the girl blessed by the Sentinel. But this girl merely nodded toward the Blessed Maiden before turning toward Cadanto. 
 
To everyone's surprise, the girl presented the bouquet to him. After some explanation from the Acolyte, we learned that Cadanto had recently saved a family from Tacet Discords near Avinoleum's outskirts. The towering Echo knight remained half-kneeling and silent. He didn't seem to understand why a human would offer him flowers, or perhaps he felt unworthy of such thanks?
 
"So this is what you've been doing in my absence…" The Blessed Maiden smiled warmly. "Cadanto, accept the flowers. You've earned them." 
 
Still silent, the knight laid down his greatsword and carefully received the bouquet. The little girl immediately leaned forward and embraced him, pressing her face against his cold armor. As always, Cadanto wordlessly bore both her tearful thanks and joyful sobs. 
 
Cadanto… as many have said, is the Blessed Maiden's loyal servant and shield. But he is also a blade that protects the people."
 
<color=Highlight>Titular Repository Memoir - Part III</color>

"…
 
Retirement drew closer with each passing day, and time flowed quietly within the library. I thought there would be no more ripples.
 
"Excuse me... I'd like to read this book. Do I need to register here?"
 
Accompanying the timid voice before me was a biography, its cover bearing the portrait of the Blessed Maiden. I looked up from the desk and saw a small girl with pale violet curls. There was a mole just beneath one of her eyes. Tiny and delicate. Her skin was so pale that it was nearly translucent like someone who hadn't seen sunlight in a very long time.
 
"You're free to read anything here. Just remember to put the books away when you're done," I said as gently as I could, worried the solemn atmosphere of the library might frighten her away.
 
She was clearly not an Avinoleum student, yet she began appearing regularly in the library in the days that followed. She wandered between the circular shelves, always quietly absorbed in whatever book she picked up. Sometimes she asked me to help her find specific texts. Some were dense theological books, while others were thick volumes on the ocean or pharmacology—not quite the usual interests for someone her age. We grew acquainted. I learned that she'd been brought to Avinoleum by her relatives. They had their own matters to attend to and left her to wander freely in this comparatively safe library.
 
Her departure was as sudden as her arrival. That afternoon, as if answering some unseen summons, she closed the book in her hands and slid it back onto the shelf. I remember it. It was a study of the traditions of the Blessed Maiden in Ragunna. In the slanting dusk light, a long shadow stretched across the floor. Her guardian, presumably.
 
"Thank you for looking after me these past few days." She stood in front of me, doing her best to smile. "Cantarella... I'm Cantarella Fisalia."
 
That surname explained a great many things. Her belated introduction. The sorrow hidden in her words. The flicker of bitterness as she looked toward the door. I rose and took her hand. At the very least, I didn't want her to feel alone on the walk back to the threshold."

Greetings, Challenger {PlayerName}.

The stars of this moment shine for you. Thank you for stepping into Colosseum Olymdos with courage and skill, and for keeping the flames of dueling alive.

I've been watching you since the moment you defeated your first opponent. Your strategy, focus, and passion, and the thoughts you put into the decks you build... all remind me of the authentic passion I once held for this game.

Challenger, fight with all your heart! On this battlefield, giving your all is the highest form of respect one duelist can offer another. No matter who will emerge victorious tomorrow, this arena belongs to both of us, two souls fighting for what they love.

May the dawn bring us to a horizon broader than yesterday's.

—Conqueror of Prestige, a fellow duelist sharing your passion.

Challenger, fight with all your heart! On this battlefield, giving your all is the highest form of respect one duelist can offer another. No matter who will emerge victorious tomorrow, this arena belongs to both of us, two souls fighting for what they love.

May the dawn bring us to a horizon broader than yesterday's.

—Conqueror of Prestige, a fellow duelist sharing your passion.

source_en:
Lupa gazes at you intensely, her eyes sparkling with passion.

"I swear by the eternal sun." It's more than a promise, but a testimonial to the lone wolf's raw loyalty and sincerity. She may be yet another soul you salvaged in your long journey. But for Lupa, she's found something she never had—something that offers the long-awaited release of her anguish and pain. You'll never know what that is, and she won't tell you either. But that's all right. For both of you, this is enough.

source_en:
Cartethyia smiles quietly. Watching her puts a smile on you, too.

After twenty years in her solitary confinement, she’s finally stepped out of that tower—back into the warmth of the crowd, into the embrace of sunlight and zephyrs. This is the moment she's been longing for through her turbulent years as the Blessed Maiden: to experience the mundanity of life, as Cartethyia, the Wandering Knight. And those three wishes she once made? They came true because you were there with her.

source_en:
This special issue offers a detailed look at the legendary figures who once shone brightly in the history of Septimont. 

From Fabius and Atilius to Valeria, tales of the Hero of Heroes occupy half the pages.

The remaining half pays tribute to those who never wore a crown, yet gave everything for the glory of Septimont. Many met their end in the hunting grounds—names like Tercules, Magna, and Taurus, lost to time, yet remembered still.

In contrast to the lyrical prose favored by Ragunnesi writers, the style here is bold and unadorned. Yet, the punchy words always evoke the most epic imagery. Though born of the same origin, the voices of Rinascita's isles have long diverged in art and expression.

source_en:
A Special Issue of The Gladiator Released Ahead of the Great Agon.

This new issue offers a look back at the storied history of past champions. From gripping duels to behind-the-scenes anecdotes, the magazine dives deep, especially in its extensive profile of current Ephor, Augusta.

But one year stands out for its omission.

That year's match ended on a strange note: the expected winner, a young girl from Ragunna, disappeared just before the award ceremony. Without receiving the victor’s medal, her win was never officially recognized.

"It’s unfortunate," the writer noted, "but without a proper conclusion, the result could never be confirmed. To this day, Mya’s standing remains a topic of debate."

source_en:
The start date of each Great Agon varies. Please refer to announcements from the Ephor's Palace for official scheduling.

Preliminaries
The preliminaries follow a points-based system, with events including but not limited to: Echo Duels, Echo Speed Tests, and Echo Teamwork Challenges. These matches test a team's overall mastery of Echoes. At the end of the preliminaries, the top 20 teams by cumulative score will advance to the Finals.

Finals
The Finals follow a single-elimination format. The top 20 teams from the preliminaries, along with specially selected teams, will face off in one-on-one matches. Winners advance until the final match determines the Champion team.

Special Qualifiers
Also held in single-elimination format, the Special Qualifiers pit participants against each other in matches involving Echo vs. Echo or Echo vs. Gladiator combat. Victors inherit the defeated side's accumulated points. Once a participant reaches the required point threshold, they earn a direct entry into the Finals.

source_en:
Yesterday, a heated dispute erupted between a noble house and a group of merchants at the small arena on Capitoline Foothills. Both parties agreed to settle matters with a duel, only for an unknown overseas team to crash the event and claim victory for themselves. Was this an innocent case of rookie misstep, or a calculated move to turn the conflict into a spectacle? Stay tuned for more on this developing story...
...
The much-anticipated 32nd Gladiator's Training Match came to an abrupt end yesterday as team Brillingsand withdrew mid-battle. Fans were left stunned, and speculation runs rampant: anonymous sources suggest that a hidden romantic relationship between the rival team members may have swayed the outcome. To add fuel to the fire, fresh rumors claim both teams may be sponsored by the same noble house, staging the drama to drum up attention for the next Great Agon...
...
With injuries piling up in recent duels, Machaon Pharmacy's medical Echo has reportedly gone missing from overwork.
If you spot an unaccompanied medical Echo wandering the streets, please contact Machaon Pharmacy immediately.
...
This paper is proudly sponsored by Vulcan Mining. Support the Vulcan Mining Gladiators!
